rows.note: Use this colloquial phrase for a brood of chicks or other young domestic fowl; it is the default choice in that context.

example.english: My grandma is raising a brood of chicks at home.
example.traditional: 阿婆屋企養住一窩雞仔。
example.jyutping: aa3 po4 uk1 kei2 joeng5 zyu6 jat1 wo1 gai1 zai2

rows.note: Use this colloquial phrase for a nestful or brood of young birds when the birds are not specifically chickens.

example.english: There is a brood of baby birds in the nest under the eaves.
example.traditional: 屋簷底嗰個雀巢有一窩鳥仔。
example.jyutping: uk1 sim4 dai2 go2 go3 zoek3 caau4 jau5 jat1 wo1 niu5 zai2

rows.traditional: 成日為咗 A 煩惱
rows.jyutping: seng4 jat6 wai6 zo2 A faan4 nou5
rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice when someone keeps dwelling moodily on A.

example.english: I brood over my job so much that I can't sleep.
example.traditional: 我成日為咗份工煩惱，搞到瞓唔着。
example.jyutping: ngo5 seng4 jat6 wai6 zo2 fan6 gung1 faan4 nou5 gaau2 dou3 fan3 m4 zoek6

rows.note: Use this specifically for keeping eggs warm so that they hatch.

example.english: The hen needs to brood over the eggs.
example.jyutping: zek3 mou5 gai1 jiu3 co5 hai2 dou6 fu1 daan2

rows.note: Use this for deliberately fostering a living thing, person, or ability as it develops rather than merely incubating an egg.

example.english: This programme is designed to brood young musicians.
example.traditional: 呢個計劃專門培育年輕音樂人。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 zyun1 mun4 pui4 juk6 nin4 heng1 jam1 ngok6 jan4
